purpose: Preregister a genuinely new-family transfer holdout for the already-frozen order-portfolio policy. No threshold, tie-break, seed rule, local-search rule, or policy action is changed after the five-family development matrix.

transferred_policy.compiler: fresh balanced-pairwise ROBDD compiler per candidate; exact rank vector and final full truth-bitset validation

seeded_diverse.choice: maximize minimum normalized Kendall distance to natural and RCM; ties lower width then lexicographic; if none eligible choose minimum-width random then lexicographic

transferred_policy.one_then_commit: run exactly one accepted-move stage independently per eligible arm, select lower live nodes; ties lower charged candidate compilations then priority RCM,natural,seeded; continue only winner up to four total accepted moves

cost_accounting: Primary cost is candidate ROBDD compilations actually paid including losing arms; final live nodes are quality. Start and final verification compilations are reported separately.

resource_guard.on_guard: mark incomplete; no local-optimum or transfer-success claim

predeclared_tests: All completed endpoints must match one family-specific exact rank vector and the direct full assignment truth bitset.
Primary transfer comparison is three_arm_one_then_commit vs full_two_arm4 on final live nodes and charged candidate compilations.
Report the count of families where three-arm is equal/better/worse quality than full-two and where it uses lower cost.
Report whether seeded_diverse is selected after one stage and whether that selected arm ultimately helps or hurts; do not relabel unselected seeded arms as successes.
Secondary comparison is two_arm_one_then_commit vs full_two_arm4 to test early-commit brittleness without the diverse third arm.
No tuning on this holdout. Any future changed threshold/seed/diversity rule requires a new protocol and a different holdout.
scope: Five previously unseen n=20 graph families relative to the development matrix. Still synthetic positive monotone 2-CNF vertex-cover formulas, not arbitrary BDD workloads or proof utility.
